entrada.texto:
Our assessment of blockchain’s effectiveness in a real-world setting is facilitated by Golang, a key tool in 
creating the consensus mechanism. This involves the setup of a complex network of three Linux laptops, six PCs, 
and a cloud server, all intricately interconnected via a local network. Each device functions as a miner, solving 
complex mathematical puzzles. The Node.js script, a crucial component, generates interactions with randomized 
locations and amounts. The script is executed by the trigger node, leading to the creation of new transactions 
that are then deposited in matching pools based on their addresses, awaiting bundling by miners. To simulate a 
W AN scenario, we manually introduce a propagation delay, with a mean value of 35–55 ms, subject to the typical 
distribution.
The blockchain’s performance is displayed in Figs. 8 and 9 for various block sizes and widths. As the width of 
the PoAh architecture grows, throughput rises with a fixed block size, as seen in Fig. 8. Meanwhile, throughput 
increases proportionally to block size growth, assuming a fixed width. Our blockchain achieves 225 tps, a 
significant improvement over Bitcoin and Ethereum, which achieves 7 tps and 27 tps respectively. The link 
between throughput in various block sizes and widths is also shown on Fig.  9. It is evident that the greater 
width and block size values of the proposed blockchain behave better than the more compact one. It reaches its

resposta.resumo: O estudo implementou uma rede de teste com laptops, PCs e um servidor cloud usando Golang e Node.js para avaliar o consenso PoAh. Foram introduzidos atrasos de propagação de 35–55 ms. Os resultados mostraram que a taxa de transferência aumenta com a largura da arquitetura e o tamanho dos blocos, atingindo 225 tps, muito superior ao Bitcoin (7 tps) e Ethereum (27 tps).
